column3: The Hebrew separately says the men came, brought the ark up, and brought it into the house. BSB combines the latter movements and leaves the upward direction implicit.
The Hebrew describes the passing of time with “the days multiplied”; BSB says “a long time passed.”
The Hebrew twice uses singular “your heart”; BSB uses plural “your hearts.”
The Hebrew introduces their words with the general “they said”; BSB specifies “they confessed.”
The Hebrew explicitly calls the advancing rulers “the rulers of the Philistines”; BSB uses “their rulers.”
The Hebrew explicitly repeats “the sons of Israel” as the speakers; BSB carries them forward as the unnamed subject of “said.”
The Hebrew repeats Samuel’s name before his crying out; BSB uses “He.”
The Hebrew says the Philistines “were defeated” before Israel; BSB says “they fled.” It describes the thunder with “a great voice,” rendered “loudly” in BSB.

The Hebrew describes the cities as returning, where BSB uses passive “were restored.” It explicitly says the Philistines had taken them from Israel and uses collective singular “the Amorite” rather than plural “the Amorites.”
The Hebrew repeats “there” for the home, the judging, and the altar-building. BSB states it for the first two and leaves it implicit for the altar.
